title: Sudan's Army-Aligned Government Rejects Abiy's Dialogue Call - RSF-Backed Administration Welcomes It
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Sudan's army-aligned government has rejected Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's invitation for an inclusive Sudanese dialogue hosted in Ethiopia, while a rival administration aligned with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has welcomed the initiative, highlighting divisions over Ethiopia's proposed role in efforts to end Sudan's war.

title: Ethiopia Vows Direct Role in Shaping Red Sea Security Architecture, Maritime Governance
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Red Sea security is an integral part of Ethiopia's national security, and the country will continue to play a direct and constructive role in regional maritime governance, Chief of Staff at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Adam Tesfaye, said.

title: Ethiopia Showcases Africa's Potential Through Tangible Milestones in Health Sector
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia is demonstrating Africa's capabilities and potential through tangible achievements and transformative progress in the healthcare sector, Minister of Health Dr. Mekdes Daba said.

title: Ethiopia, Pakistan Agree to Deepen Defence and Aviation Cooperation
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia and Pakistan have agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation in defence and aviation, opening further avenues for strategic partnership between the two countries.

title: Obasanjo to Chair Sasakawa Africa Association's 40th Anniversary Symposium in Addis Ababa
summary: [Nile Post] Former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo is set to chair the Sasakawa Africa Association's (SAA) 40th anniversary symposium scheduled for December 1-2, 2026, in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, bringing together African leaders, policymakers, agricultural experts and development partners to discuss the future of the continent's food and nutrition security.

title: Somalia's Parliament Speaker Accuses Kenya, Ethiopia, Uganda of Colluding With Al-Shabaab
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Somalia's parliamentary speaker Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur, also known as Jaamac, has accused Kenya, Ethiopia and Uganda of colluding with Al-Shabaab, alleging that Israel had brought together the three countries, the militant group and forces loyal to former South West State leader Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen in a coordinated front against the federal government.

title: Ethiopia Intensifies Efforts to Expand Earning From Pulses and Oilseeds, Sector Contributes $572.9 Million
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia, which has earned about 5 percent of the country's total export from pulses and oilseeds last Ethiopian fiscal year, is stepping up efforts to expand the earning through economic reforms, investment promotion, improved product quality and value addition, Trade and Regional Integration Minister Yasmin Wohabrebbi said.

title: Arkwood Africa Film Market and Awards Forum to Take Place in Addis Ababa
summary: [ENA] The second edition of Arkwood Africa Film Market and Awards will be held at Adwa Victory Memorial Museum in Addis Ababa from November 27-28, 2026, according to Ministry of Culture and Tourism.

title: PM Abiy Invites All Sudanese Parties to Inclusive Dialogue, Offers Ethiopia As Host for Peace Talks
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has extended an open invitation to all Sudanese military, political and civilian parties to participate in an inclusive national dialogue hosted and facilitated by Ethiopia, calling for an end to the devastating war and a Sudanese-led path toward lasting peace.

title: Strategic Location Qualifies Ethiopia to Invigorate Trade Connectivity in Continent - Egyptian Comesa Expert
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- An Egyptian expert at the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) has described Ethiopia as a "Land of Origin," highlighting its strategic location as a vital link between markets in Eastern, Western and Central Africa.

title: PM Abiy to Address Parliament On Government Performance, National Priorities Thursday
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed is set to appear at the House of Peoples' Representatives on Thursday to present the federal government's performance during the 2026/27 Ethiopian fiscal year's quarter and respond to lawmakers' questions on key national issues.

title: Ethiopia Urges Egypt to Modernize Water Use, Consult On Nile Development Projects
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia's Minister of Water and Energy, Habtamu Itefa, has urged Egypt to modernize its domestic water management practices and reconsider water-intensive agricultural activities that have resulted in excessive water wastage in the downstream country.

title: Ethiopia Launches Polio Vaccination Campaign Targeting 11.3 Million Children
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia has launched a polio vaccination campaign targeting more than 11.3 million children across five regions, amid continued outbreaks of circulating variant poliovirus that threaten children in areas with gaps in immunization coverage.

title: Ethiopia, Djibouti Discuss Port Efficiency, Trade Corridor Improvements Ahead of Next Rainy Season
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia and Djibouti have discussed improving port productivity, transport corridor efficiency and trade facilitation, as the two countries seek to strengthen the logistics network underpinning Ethiopia's dependence on Djibouti for international maritime trade.

title: Artillery Strikes On Alamata Civilians in Tigray Region Must Be Investigated As War Crimes: Amnesty
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Artillery strikes by Ethiopian federal forces and allied Tigray Peace Forces (TPF) that killed civilians and injured many others in Alamata, southern Tigray, in late September must be investigated as possible war crimes, Amnesty International said, while also accusing TPLF forces of placing civilians at risk by establishing military bases in populated neighborhoods, including schools.

title: Territorial Disputes, Drought and Dwindling Resources Fuel Renewed Fighting and Displacement Along Ethiopia's Afar-Somali Border
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A conflict long rooted in contested territorial claims, fragile political agreements, and competing regional administrations is once again threatening communities along the Afar-Somali border, where renewed armed clashes, restrictions on grazing and access to water, and mounting displacement are deepening an already protracted crisis.

title: Ethiopia, Norway Vow to Deepen Strategic Partnership On Climate Action and Sustainable Development
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia and Norway have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation on climate finance, forest conservation and multilateral development partnerships.

title: African Leaders Call for Action, Domestic Investment to Advance Health Sovereignty
summary: [ENA] African leaders have called for stronger political commitment, increased domestic investment and concrete action to accelerate the continent's transition toward health sovereignty, self-reliance and resilient healthcare systems.

title: Ethiopia's Deputy PM Urges African Nations to Move Beyond Raw Material Exports, Boost Value Addition
summary: [ENA] Ethiopia's Deputy Prime Minister Temesgen Tiruneh has urged African countries to move beyond exporting raw materials and accelerate value addition, industrialization and intra-African trade to translate the continent's economic potential into jobs, prosperity and improved living standards.

Over the past decade, ties between the two countries have swung repeatedly from close cooperation to deep suspicion, open confrontation, and fragile reconciliation. title: United Bank for Africa Shelved Ethiopia Banking Expansion Over Nigeria's 10% Foreign Investment Cap
summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Nigerian billionaire businessman Tony Elumelu has disclosed that United Bank for Africa (UBA) was unable to pursue its ambition of becoming the first international bank to operate in Ethiopia after Nigeria's central bank enforced a regulatory cap limiting banks' investments in foreign subsidiaries to 10% of their capital.

title: Lethal Artillery Strikes On Civilian Neighbourhoods in Tigray's Alamata City Must Be Investigated As War Crimes
summary: [AI London] Artillery attacks by Ethiopia's military and its allied Tigray Peace Forces (TPF) that killed dozens of civilians and injured many more in the city of Alamata in the northern region of Tigray, between 26 and 28 September, must be investigated as possible war crimes, Amnesty International said today.

title: Health Financing Top of Agenda As African Leaders Meet in Addis
summary: [New Times] African leaders and health experts began a five-day meeting in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, on Monday, November 23, to discuss ways of reducing the continent's dependence on foreign health financing and imported medical supplies.

title: Ethiopia Wins Seat On Expanded UN Aviation Council With 133 Votes
summary: [Horn Diplomat] Ethiopia has been elected to the governing council of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), winning 133 votes in a ballot that filled four new seats at the United Nations aviation agency.

title: PM Abiy Holds High-Level Bilateral Talks With African and UAE Leaders On Cphia 2026 Sidelines
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has held a series of high-level bilateral meetings with African leaders and a senior United Arab Emirates official on the sidelines of the Fifth International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026), exploring avenues to deepen diplomatic relations, expand economic cooperation and advance shared regional and continental priorities.

title: Africa Pushes for Transformation From Health Dependency to Self-Reliance
summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- As the Fifth International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026) gets underway in Addis Ababa, Africa is pushing for a fundamental transformation of its health sector, moving away from dependency and vulnerability toward greater ownership, self-reliance and resilience.

title: COP31 Ends in Deadlock, Leaving Ethiopia to Pick Up the Pieces
summary: [IPS] Antalya, Türkiye -- There is no final cover decision at this year's United Nations climate summit after countries did not agree on a text that explicitly mentions moving away from fossil fuels.
